overview: CAT is the single gateway exam for the **21 Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs)** and well over a thousand other MBA and PGDM programs across India — from FMS Delhi to the IITs' management schools. One IIM conducts it each year on rotation, as a **120-minute computer-based test** with three time-locked sections (VARC, DILR, QA — 40 minutes each) held in **three slots on one Sunday** in late November. There is no pass or fail: your scaled score becomes a **percentile**, and every institute builds its own shortlist from that percentile plus your academics, work experience and diversity factors, followed by WAT/GD and PI rounds. Around 3 lakh candidates register each year for a few thousand IIM seats, so the real game is **percentile maximisation** — sectional strategy, accuracy and timed mocks — not generic study.

stages.name: CAT — Computer-Based Test
stages.nature: Screening — no pass/fail; the scaled percentile feeds institute shortlists
stages.mode: Online CBT · 3 slots on one day
stages.negative: +3 per correct · −1 per wrong MCQ · no negative for TITA
stages.notes: Section order is fixed — **VARC first, then DILR, then QA** — with **40 minutes locked per section**: you cannot move between sections or bank time. The counts above are the **CAT 2025 paper** (held 30 November 2025): VARC was 4 RC passages of 4 questions each plus 8 verbal-ability items; DILR had about five sets (4–5 questions each); QA spread arithmetic (the biggest chunk), algebra, geometry, number systems and modern maths. IIMs do **not** pre-announce question counts, so treat 24/22/22 as the baseline and confirm from the first analysis after exam day. Question types: standard MCQs plus **TITA (Type In The Answer)** items in all three sections — TITA carries no negative marking. PwD candidates get 160 minutes (about 53 minutes 20 seconds per section). An **on-screen basic calculator** is provided; physical devices are banned. All three slots run on the same day with different papers, and scores are scaled across slots.

stages.name: Institute-level selection (IIMs and other colleges)
stages.negative: Composite weights vary by institute — the CAT percentile is typically 40–65% of the shortlist score
stages.notes: Every institute publishes its own admission policy after the CAT result. Shortlists typically combine the **scaled CAT percentile (with overall and sectional minimums)** against your Class 10, Class 12 and graduation marks, work experience and gender/academic-diversity factors — for example, IIM Ahmedabad's PGP shortlist weights the **CAT percentile 65% and an Application Rating (10th/12th/graduation scores) 35%**, leading to AWT + PI. Clearing a published minimum percentile does **not** guarantee a call — effective shortlist cutoffs run far higher (see the cutoffs page). Final offers follow WAT/GD and PI performance, with Government of India reservation norms applied category-wise.

eligibility.nationality: Citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962 with permanent settlement intent, or a person of Indian origin migrated from the countries listed in the official notification.

education.requirement: Bachelor's degree (any discipline) of at least 3 years with a minimum of **50% marks or equivalent CGPA** (45% for SC, ST and PwD candidates). Professional degrees such as CA, CS and ICWA are accepted.

Eligible to apply provisionally — the degree (or completion certificate) must be produced by the deadline each institute sets, typically around June of the admission year; failure converts the provisional admission to cancellation
Aggregate of all years/semesters as computed by the admitting institute — follow the method stated in each IIM's admission policy for rounding and CGPA conversion

age.range: No age limit — you may attempt CAT in as many years as you wish

eligibility.notes: The 50%/45% degree bar is CAT's own eligibility floor; individual institutes may add stricter requirements (extra minimums, discipline-specific criteria for programs like IIM Lucknow's ABM or IIM Indore's PGP-HRM) in their admission policies. Reservation for SC, ST, NC-OBC, EWS and PwD categories applies at the IIMs per Government of India norms, with correspondingly lower qualifying percentiles. Always read the official notification and the target institute's admission policy — they override any summary, including this one.

selectionProcess: **CAT exam → scaled score and percentile → institute-wise shortlists (composite: CAT percentile + academics + work experience + diversity) → WAT/GD + Personal Interview → final admission offers.** The exam has no passing score — your percentile is only the entry ticket. Each IIM (and every other college accepting CAT) publishes its own admission policy with qualifying minimums (overall and sectional), composite-score weightings and reservation norms. Shortlists land between December and February; WAT/GD-PI rounds run through February–April; offers and waitlist movement continue into the summer. The CAT score itself is **valid for one admission cycle only**.
normalization: Because CAT runs in three slots on one day with different question papers, raw scores are converted to **scaled (equated) scores** — a statistical adjustment for slot difficulty — and percentiles are computed from the scaled scores. Your **percentile** (the share of candidates at or below your score) is the only number institutes see, along with sectional percentiles. Practical consequences: (1) never compare raw marks across slots or years; (2) maximise attempts where your slot's paper is soft — scaling protects you in a hard slot but doesn't reward complacency in an easy one; (3) sectional percentiles matter as much as the overall figure because most IIMs set per-section minimums for shortlists.

faqs.q: What is the negative marking in CAT?
faqs.a: Each correct answer earns **+3 marks**. Each wrong **MCQ** costs **−1**. Wrong **TITA (Type In The Answer)** questions carry **no negative marking**, and skipped questions cost nothing — so always attempt every TITA, but be selective about MCQ guesses.

faqs.q: What was the CAT 2025 pattern — how many questions per section?
faqs.a: The CAT 2025 paper (30 November 2025) had **68 questions in 120 minutes**: **VARC 24, DILR 22, QA 22**, 40 minutes locked per section, maximum **204 marks**. The same 3-section, 2-hour frame has held since CAT 2021; question counts changed across those years (66 in 2023, 68 in 2024 and 2025) and are never announced in advance.

faqs.q: Is there a limit on CAT attempts?
faqs.a: No. There is **no attempt limit and no age limit** — you can appear in as many years as you like, as long as you hold (or are completing) a bachelor's degree with the required 50% (45% for SC/ST/PwD).

Yes — provisionally. You must produce your degree or completion certificate by the deadline each admitting institute sets (typically around June of the admission year). If you can't, the admission lapses.

faqs.q: Do I need a sectional cutoff in CAT itself?
faqs.a: The exam has **no pass/fail and no sectional cutoff of its own** — but sections are time-locked at 40 minutes each, and most IIMs set **sectional percentile minimums** in their admission policies when building shortlists. So a lopsided scorecard (huge QA, tiny VARC) can disqualify you from many shortlists even with a strong overall percentile.

faqs.q: How does the score-to-percentile conversion work?
faqs.a: Raw scores are first scaled across the three slots to equalise difficulty, then converted to percentiles. As an indicative benchmark compiled from the **actual CAT 2025 results**: roughly **85 scaled marks (out of 204) landed at the 99th percentile**, about **62 at the 95th** and about **51 at the 90th**. These bands shift every year with paper difficulty and the candidate pool — treat them as ranges, never targets.

faqs.q: Is 99 percentile enough for IIM Ahmedabad, Bangalore or Calcutta?
faqs.a: It makes you genuinely competitive — General-category shortlists at the top three IIMs typically land in the **98.5–99.5+ percentile** band. But shortlisting is a **composite score** (CAT percentile plus academics, work experience and diversity factors), and final offers depend further on WAT/GD-PI. A 99-percentiler with weak Class 12 marks can miss a shortlist that a 97-percentiler with strong academics makes.

faqs.q: What percentile do I need for the newer IIMs and FMS Delhi?
faqs.a: For the **newer IIMs via CAP**, General-category shortlists typically form in the **90–96 percentile** band. **FMS Delhi** historically shortlists around **98–99 percentile** (General) on a composite of CAT score and Class 10/12 marks. Reserved-category bands run well below these — see the cutoffs page for category-wise ranges.

Type In The Answer — questions with no options to choose from; you key the answer in directly. They appear in all three sections and carry **no negative marking**. Even a rough guess on TITA has positive expected value, so never leave them blank.

faqs.q: Is a calculator allowed in CAT?
faqs.a: A basic **on-screen calculator** is built into the test interface. Physical calculators, phones, smartwatches and all other electronic devices are banned. Mental-maths speed (fractions, percentages, squares, approximations) is still a scored skill — the calculator is too slow for the volume you need to attempt.

faqs.q: Can I choose my exam slot or city?
faqs.a: You indicate preferred test cities in the application form, but the **slot and final city are allocated by the conducting IIM** and appear only on your admit card. CAT 2026 runs three slots on 29 November 2026 — you cannot pick which one you get.

faqs.q: How long is a CAT score valid?
faqs.a: One admission cycle. A CAT 2026 score is usable for the 2027-28 batch admissions only — there is no carry-forward to the next year.

faqs.q: What happens after the CAT result?
faqs.a: Each institute releases its own **shortlist** using its published composite formula, then runs **WAT (Written Ability Test) or GD (Group Discussion) plus a Personal Interview**, and makes final offers. The older IIMs run their own rounds, most newer IIMs share the **CAP** common WAT-PI, and non-IIM colleges (FMS, IITs and hundreds of others) run parallel processes on the same score — so apply widely rather than betting on one institute.

faqs.q: When are the CAT 2026 admit card and result released?
faqs.a: The admit card is expected on **4 November 2026** on iimcat.ac.in. The provisional answer key and response sheet typically follow in about 1–2 weeks, and the result around **late December 2026 – January 2027** (CAT 2025's result came on 24 December 2025; CAT 2024's on 19 December 2024).

documents: On exam day you need the **admit card printout** (colour recommended) plus **one original photo ID** — Aadhaar, PAN, passport, driving licence or voter ID — with the name and date of birth exactly matching your registration; e-copies on phones are not accepted. For the **WAT/GD-PI and admission stage**, keep ready: Class 10 and Class 12 certificates and marksheets, all **graduation marksheets** and the degree/provisional certificate, the **category certificate** (SC/ST/NC-OBC/EWS in the Government of India format, current validity), **PwD certificate** where applicable, work-experience letters, and passport photographs. Name or DOB mismatches across documents are the classic shortlist-stage headache — resolve them with a gazette notification or affidavit before interviews, not after an offer is questioned.
